status_summary: H.R. 1602, the Financial Privacy Act of 2025, was ordered reported 48 to 0 on 2025-03-05 and reported by the House Financial Services Committee on 2025-03-21, and it remains on the Union Calendar with no floor or Senate action recorded. Its Sec. 3 would require the Treasury Secretary to report annually to the House and Senate committees on the number of reports filed with FinCEN by type and the number retained, expiring after seven years; it does not require public data or reporting on prosecutions, convictions, fines or compliance costs. FinCEN published a proposed rule on anti-money laundering programs on 2026-04-10, citing Executive Order 14192 and aiming to reduce compliance burdens; it does not require the annual data, the FinCEN and GAO evaluations, or the retrospective review the chapter describes. Committee leaders urged FinCEN on 2026-06-09 to finalize that rule with reduced burdens.

timeline.event: The House Financial Services Committee ordered H.R. 1602 reported, as amended, by a vote of 48 to 0.

The House Financial Services Committee reported H.R. 1602, the Financial Privacy Act of 2025 (H. Rept. 119-24), and the bill was placed on the Union Calendar; its Sec. 3 would require the Treasury Secretary to report annually to the House and Senate committees on the number of reports filed with FinCEN by type since 2022 and the number retained, with the provision repealed after seven years.
FinCEN published a proposed rule reforming anti-money laundering program requirements and citing regulatory burden reduction.
House Financial Services Committee Republican leaders sent FinCEN a letter urging a final rule with reduced compliance burdens and higher report filing thresholds (reported 2026-06-26).

BILLSTATUS shows no House floor passage or Senate action through the run date. The 2026-04-10 proposed rule was read in full in an earlier pass and not reopened; the researcher's Federal Register listing of FinCEN documents since 2026-04-01 shows no final program rule and no retrospective review document. The CBO estimate remains a source but its wording on suspicious activity reports is a reading of the bill. The FinCEN SAR statistics page prints no date and was not treated as evidence. The legislators' letter is a dated official act but does not advance the specific items.
